[L]'s only order statements in this chain are YM.Stationary.Rays, defined as `(fun t => f (t • x)) =O[cutRay] (fun t => t^s)`, which scales the field amplitude and so measures jet (Taylor-degree) order of the whole function, not momentum order of a fixed-degree vertex; top_Wilson concludes `Rays 3 (WilsonQ G m - inputSeries u p)` and assembly/orbit_gate take `Rays 3` hypotheses and conclude `Rays 5`, i.e. agreement through degree four. No declaration states momentum vanishing orders 3,2,1 for the degree-2,3,4 differences, so the identities, kernel bounds and matching are in [L] but the momentum-order claim is not, and the claim stands. It is a substantive statement, not a typo.

The claim's finding is that nothing in [L] states [M]'s last sentence, that the degree-r fine-minus-Wilson vertex has momentum order 5-r for r=2,3,4. YM.Stationary.greyson states exactly this: under the bed, floor, strip and attachment hypotheses it concludes `∀ i, i>0 → i≤3 → Drinkable i m (fun i => intended p R - WilsonQ G (m i)) (4-i) s M`. Drinkable gives a degree-(i+1) Taylor picture Q, Recorded against intended-minus-Wilson, with `Rays (4-i) (Q i j ∘ axes)`, i.e. vanishing to order 4-i in momentum, which is 5-r for r=i+1. The companion lemma whiteWilson gives Wilson's orders 3-k (=4-r), as in [M]'s proof, and setWest uses both through voile G 2 2 and voile G 3 1. The other claims (the D^3/D^4 identities in triumph3/triumph4, with the completed inverse that [M] identifies with Q^-1 via Lemma B5; the C_3/6 and (C_4+3C_3^2E)/24 bounds in pennies/exchangeYield; the degree-four agreement in assembly/transition_cap) are conceded by the claim, so the item is covered in parts.
